Looking at this issue, the problem is that when a test dynamically adds an xfail marker during test execution (via `request.node.add_marker()`), pytest 6 no longer handles it properly. The issue is that `evaluate_xfail_marks()` is called in `pytest_runtest_setup`, but if the marker is added during the test function itself, it won't be picked up.

The fix should ensure that `evaluate_xfail_marks()` is called again during `pytest_runtest_call` if the xfail evaluation hasn't been done yet or if it was None. Looking at the code, I can see that `pytest_runtest_call` already has logic to re-evaluate xfail marks, but it only does so when `xfailed is None`. The problem is that in `pytest_runtest_setup`, `xfailed_key` is always set (either to an `Xfail` object or `None`), so the re-evaluation in `pytest_runtest_call` never triggers.

The fix is to not store `None` in `xfailed_key` during setup, so that the call hook can re-evaluate when markers might have been added dynamically.
